messages:
Devin Park: Quick heads-up — I pushed the kernel auto-swap for qwen-7b (enable tiled-attn fast path) to canary yesterday. Microbenchmarks looked great but long-context evals show a quality regression and some KV-cache errors. Posting quick perf/eval excerpts below.

Devin Park: perf diff (canary vs baseline):
```
p50: 32ms -> 28ms
p95: 68ms -> 95ms
throughput (tok/s): 12k -> 14.3k
cost/token: -12%
```
Devin Park: eval summary: LongChatBench rouge -2.3, hallucination rate +1.8%, several failures at seq_len 2k+. Logs show KV restore shape mismatch in some traces: `kv_cache_restore: expected heads=32 got 16` :thinking:

Marta Chen: Which evals exactly? RoPE scaling or attention swap? That kv error looks like a head/kv-dim mismatch to me.

Devin Park: LongChatBench + internal perf-evals. Repro trace attached that shows kv indices shifted after first restore. Not convinced it's RoPE scaling alone — more like stride/packing assumption in tiled kernel.

Sanjay Rao: If the tiled kernel assumes `head_dim` packing of 64 and qwen variant uses 32, we could be misinterpreting kv stride. Did the kernel rely on `num_heads` multiple? We tested tiled mostly on mixtral/mistral where heads % 8 == 0.

Ryan Li: We only ran tiled on models with head dim multiples we control. For qwen the implementation changed the kv buffer layout (packed heads) which can lead to wrong offsets on restore if `kv_stride` computed differently. Repro steps: 
```bash
# repro locally
./bin/serve --model qwen-7b --kernel auto-swap --enable-tiled \
  --test-seq 2048 --trace-kv > kv_trace.log
./tools/kv_check --input kv_trace.log --assert-shapes
```
Expect failure on kv_check for some seeds.

Devin Park: I ran that locally, got `kv_cache_restore: shape mismatch (32,64) vs (16,128)` then downstream attention indexing misaligned. Also saw tiny float diffs bigger after int8 path active.

Marta Chen: Can we rollback tiled kernel for qwen quickly? We should flip per-model flag until we fix. + add a runtime guard that disables tiled when head_dim or kv_dim aren't aligned.

perf-bot: Rollback action recorded: reverted kernel auto-swap for `qwen-7b` on pool-redwood-a at 2026-03-17T14:05Z by @Devin Park (reason: quality-regression detected by LongChatBench). :white_check_mark:

Sanjay Rao: Also check that quantization toggle (fast int8) wasn't on in the same canary build — combining int8 + tiled packed layout can amplify small numerical shifts into visible quality regressions. If so, revert quant path too.

Ryan Li: Plan: add shape/assert in `kv_restore()` and a runtime guard: `if (num_heads % 8 != 0 || head_dim % 64 != 0) disable_tiled_kernel = true`. Add unit that simulates restore with interleaved vs contiguous layouts. I'll also add an integration test that runs LongChatBench subset on canary.

Marta Chen: Good. Also schedule a short canary (2h) that collects both perf and evaluation metrics; compare rouge/hallucination against baseline before broad rollout. Tagging @perf for p95 and quality hooks.

Devin Park: Logged rollback PR and incident note. Short TL;DR: tiled kernel improved cost but broke kv layout assumptions for qwen variants (head/kv mismatch + int8 path interaction). Revert per-model until guard+tests landed. Thanks all. :pray:
